name: Ross Buhrdorf
profile: Nebraska-born technologist who was founding CTO of HomeAway (vacation rentals), acquired by Expedia for $3.9B in 2015. That year he co-founded ZenBusiness with Shanaz Hemmati, a public-benefit SaaS platform for business formation and compliance that has served 1M+ entrepreneurs and reached a ~$1.7-2B valuation.
interesting_fact: He met his ZenBusiness co-founder Shanaz Hemmati when both worked at Excite.com, one of the internet's earliest web portals; EY named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Gulf South) in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: His personal motto, published on ZenBusiness's site: "Fear is a liar that holds us back... Don't let fear dictate your actions - go for it."
notes: Best route is ZenBusiness press team. Company is a PBC; Hemmati is also co-founder.

name: Assaf Eisenstein
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Lusha, a B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform, with developer Yoni Tserruya in 2016. Lusha bootstrapped to profitability before raising a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation; Eisenstein oversees business operations (legal, finance, investment strategy) as president.
interesting_fact: Lusha began as a side project aimed at recruiters, but salespeople quickly became its main users; it grew from a Chrome extension into a data platform with 515M+ data entries and now an MCP/API layer for AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lusha he was an HR-tech founder (Lusha's own site calls him 'an HR tech creator'), having built employee-referral software in Tel Aviv - which is why Lusha was first pitched as a recruiting tool.
notes: Low public profile compared to CEO Yoni Tserruya. No published press email found; LinkedIn (linked from Lusha's About page) is best route. Lusha's name comes from a family nickname (avoid in outreach per rules).

name: Eric Cheng
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & Group CEO, CARSOME (Kuala Lumpur)
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur who co-founded CARSOME in 2015 with Innity colleague Teoh Jiun Ee. It grew into Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform (Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore) and Malaysia's first tech unicorn, valued around $1.7B in 2021. He leads group strategy and sits on Endeavor Malaysia's board.
interesting_fact: An accounting-degree dropout, Cheng says he 'wasn't the smartest kid in the family'; Carsome was his third company after two short-lived ventures. He was EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year Malaysia 2019.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he started Clicks Communications, an ad network and creative agency, but sold his stake back to his co-founders within a year because he felt he had left Innity too soon - and went back to lead Innity's digital ad team before founding Carsome. His first venture (2008) was a print magazine with college friends.
notes: Active in SEA startup community and Endeavor Malaysia; Endeavor is a possible warm route.

name: Matan Ben-Gur
current_role: Co-founder of Orca Security (previously Chief Architect; current operational role unconfirmed); angel investor
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (Tel Aviv, founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company built on 'SideScanning', which raised ~$630M and was valued at $1.8B. A Tel Aviv University alumnus and Check Point Software veteran like most of the founding team, he served as Orca's Chief Architect and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Orca's founders largely came out of Check Point Software; the company reached unicorn status within about two years of launching its product in 2019.
notes: Very low public profile; not listed on Orca's current leadership page and some insider databases list his Orca role as former. No published personal contact found; route via Orca Security's PR team or LinkedIn. Database bios conflict on whether he or Liran Antebi held the Chief Architect title.

name: Peter Meusel
current_role: Co-Founder, Agile Robots SE (Munich); role beyond co-founder not confirmed (TheOrg lists Co-CEO/Managing Director)
profile: German robotics engineer from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) who co-founded Agile Robots in 2018 with Dr. Zhaopeng Chen and eight other DLR experts. The Munich-based DLR spin-off builds force-sensitive robot arms, hands and AI-driven automation systems and has become one of Europe's most valuable robotics companies, backed by Sequoia China, Hillhouse and others.
interesting_fact: Agile Robots' first robot, the seven-axis lightweight arm 'Diana 7', debuted in 2019, only a year after founding; the company has since moved into humanoids and 'physical AI'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agile Robots, Meusel and Chen co-founded an earlier DLR spin-off, Wessling Robotics, built on the humanoid robot hand Chen developed at DLR; Meusel is also credited as a key member of the team behind the DLR/KUKA Light-Weight Robot (LWR).
notes: Low public profile; CEO Zhaopeng Chen is the company's public face. LWR credit comes from his Crunchbase profile (https://www.crunchbase.com/person/peter-meusel). No published press email found on the JS-rendered site.

name: Kevin Chou
current_role: Founding CEO/Chairman of Forte; Managing Partner, SuperLayer (crypto venture studio, Palo Alto); co-founder of Rally
profile: UC Berkeley alum (BS 2002) and ex-Deutsche Bank banker / Canaan Partners VC who co-founded Kabam, the mobile game maker (Kingdoms of Camelot, Marvel Contest of Champions) whose assets were sold in 2016-17 for roughly $800M-$900M. He then led Gen.G Esports, founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte (valued ~$1B in 2021) and co-founded Rally and the SuperLayer venture studio.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Kabam signed an $18M deal with UC Berkeley that included naming rights to Kabam Field at California Memorial Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife pledged up to $25M to Berkeley Haas - the largest gift ever from a Haas alum under 40 - and the resulting Connie & Kevin Chou Hall became the first US academic building certified TRUE Zero Waste at the platinum level (2019).
notes: Forte CEO title passed to co-founder Josh Williams; Chou's current focus appears to be SuperLayer/Rally. Kabam's first product was Watercooler, a fantasy-sports social network (2006) that pivoted to Facebook games. No verified personal/press email found.

name: Thomas Clozel
profile: French oncologist-hematologist (MD) and former clinical assistant professor at Hopital Henri-Mondor who co-founded Owkin in 2016 with ML professor Gilles Wainrib. Owkin applies AI and federated learning to drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a $180M Sanofi investment, and now pitches 'biological artificial superintelligence' via its K Pro AI-scientist agent.
interesting_fact: Owkin has raised 300M+ dollars and signed AI deals with Sanofi, BMS, Servier, MSD and AstraZeneca; it released K Pro, an agentic 'AI scientist' for biology, in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before medicine he flirted with moving to LA 'to crack Hollywood'. He landed his Weill Cornell lab spot by meeting Ari Melnick in a Deauville hotel lobby: his phone had died, so he scanned the room until he spotted a man sipping a Diet Coke while reading a cell-biology paper.
notes: Son of Actelion founders Jean-Paul and Martine Clozel. Frequent conference speaker on AI in biology; Owkin press team is the clear route.

name: Stephan Wolf
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (Bruchsal, Germany); current role not publicly documented
profile: German industrial-automation software specialist who co-founded Volocopter (originally e-volo) in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Alexander Zosel and Thomas Senkel. Volocopter pioneered electric multicopter air taxis and reached a ~$2B valuation, but filed for insolvency in December 2024 and was acquired in 2025 by Diamond Aircraft (owned by China's Wanfeng).
interesting_fact: Volocopter's first prototype, the VC1, was essentially a seat on a yoga ball with 16 electric rotors; its 90-second flight on 21 Oct 2011 is credited as the world's first crewed all-electric multicopter flight.
deep_cut_fact: The Volocopter idea was Wolf's: in 2010, after being struck by how stable a small consumer quadcopter was, he did his own calculations on scaling it up to carry people and then pitched the project to his childhood friend Alex Zosel, a hobby pilot and paragliding instructor.
notes: Very low public profile; no current role, personal site or social accounts found. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (no reports of death). Volocopter no longer independent, so the company press office is not a reliable route to him.

name: Ravi Saraogi
profile: Indian entrepreneur who co-founded Uniphore with college batchmate Umesh Sachdev in 2008 at IIT Madras's Rural Technology & Business Incubator. Uniphore grew from Indian-language speech recognition for rural users into an enterprise conversational/business-AI platform, raising $400M in 2022 at a $2.5B valuation; Saraogi leads APAC sales and delivery from Singapore.
interesting_fact: Uniphore's first customer was Thomson Reuters' Reuters Market Light farmer-information service: pilots showed low rural literacy made SMS ineffective, so the team built voice-based systems in Indian languages instead.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006, as batchmates at Jaypee Institute of Information Technology in Noida, he and Sachdev first experimented with a mobile anti-theft security product and founded Singularis Technologies, turning down software-services job offers to pursue it.
notes: Education is reported inconsistently (Uniphore bio: MSc Mathematics, Delhi University; other profiles: B.Tech IT, Jaypee). CEO Umesh Sachdev is the company's main public face. No published press email found on Uniphore's site.

name: Alex Kinnier
profile: Lehigh chemical engineer and Harvard MBA who worked as a Google product manager and as SVP of Products & Engineering at energy-efficiency software firm Opower (sold to Oracle for $532M) before co-founding Upside with Opower colleague Wayne Lin in 2015. Upside's cash-back app and personalized-offer platform for gas stations, grocers and restaurants reached a ~$1.5-2B valuation and 50,000+ partner locations.
interesting_fact: Upside started at gas stations - by 2017 it was live at about 650 stations around D.C. and Baltimore - and now partners with fuel brands including bp, Shell, Circle K, Phillips 66 and Valero.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Upside came from Google chief economist Hal Varian's theory that brick-and-mortar retail is hugely inefficient compared with data-personalized e-commerce, which Kinnier encountered as a Google product manager. His Opower stint (data-driven home energy reports for utilities) is a natural energy-podcast hook.
notes: Has been quoted by Fortune on gas-station margins and fuel prices; comfortable with energy/fuel retail topics. Opower title per aggregator profiles (Clay/MarketScreener).

name: Conor McCarthy
profile: Irish software developer who co-founded Flipdish with his brother James in 2015, after earlier running software firm SawdeeSoft. Flipdish provides online ordering apps, kiosks and POS for takeaway and delivery restaurants; it became an Irish unicorn in 2022 with a $94M Tiger Global-led round at a ~$1.25B valuation, and McCarthy now focuses it on UK and Irish operators.
interesting_fact: He holds both the CEO and CTO titles at Flipdish, and his core business advice is to never do anything 'because it's standard' - everything, contracts included, is negotiable.
deep_cut_fact: He's a keen mountain biker on the Dublin Mountains trails and says it teaches a business lesson: focus on the 'happy path', not the rocks and trees, i.e. on what could go right rather than what could go wrong. His life mantra: 'Live and let live.'
notes: Co-founder brother James McCarthy (CRO/CCO) is more often the commercial face. No published press email found on Flipdish site.

name: Geng Shusheng
current_role: Co-founder, JOINN Biologics; listed as founder/director linked to JOINN Laboratories (China) (exact current title unconfirmed)
profile: Chinese biologics executive listed by Crunchbase as co-founder of JOINN Biologics, with 20+ years in biological macromolecule drug R&D and management, and by MarketScreener as a founder/director tied to JOINN Laboratories (China) and JOINN Biologics (HK). JOINN Biologics is the biologics CDMO offshoot of Shanghai/HK-listed preclinical CRO JOINN Labs, with US plants in Richmond and Sacramento, California; it raised $150M in 2021.
interesting_fact: JOINN Biologics was spun out of JOINN Laboratories, one of China's largest preclinical safety-evaluation CROs (listed in Shanghai, 603127, and Hong Kong, 6127), to manufacture antibodies and other biologics for drug developers.
notes: Very thin public footprint; only data-aggregator profiles (Crunchbase, MarketScreener) found, none independently confirming his title. JOINN group's public face is founder/chair Feng Yuxia. No contacts found; route via JOINN Laboratories IR (HK/Shanghai listed) would need verification.

name: Piyush Prahladka
current_role: Co-founder of Glean (former Head of Search & AI); reportedly Co-Founder & CEO of a stealth enterprise work-management/AI startup in Palo Alto since Feb 2024
profile: Engineer who spent over a decade at Google, then worked at Uber, before co-founding Glean in 2019 with Arvind Jain (Rubrik co-founder), T.R. Vishwanath and Tony Gentilcore. He led search and AI for Glean's enterprise search / work-AI assistant, which was valued at $7.2B in 2025. He left around 2023 to start a new company.
interesting_fact: Glean was born from Arvind Jain's frustration at Rubrik, where a survey found that finding information was employees' 'single biggest' workplace problem across 300+ SaaS apps.
deep_cut_fact: At Google (2005-2017) he was a technical/engineering lead on the Google Maps and Search Quality Ranking teams, the background that shaped Glean's ranking engine for enterprise search.
notes: Post-Glean venture unclear: one aggregator says a stealth work-management startup, another names it Aida (AI chief of staff for sales). No verified personal site or contact found. Glean's earlier Uber work (Uber Transit, shared bikes) is per startupintros.com aggregator only.

name: Roth Martin
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Creative and Innovation Officer, Rothy's (San Francisco) - since Jan 2024, previously President
profile: San Francisco native and former gallery owner who co-founded Rothy's with ex-investment banker Stephen Hawthornthwaite. Rothy's makes washable 3D-knit shoes and bags from recycled plastic bottles in its own factory on a make-to-demand model, and reached a ~$1B valuation. In Jan 2024 he moved from president to chief creative and innovation officer.
interesting_fact: Rothy's debuted its recycled-bottle flats in the vegetable aisle of San Francisco's Ferry Plaza Farmers Market, between eggplants and Brussels sprouts, after four years of development that nearly sank the company.
deep_cut_fact: He came to shoes as a former San Francisco gallery owner, not a footwear person. On Rothy's early struggles: 'We had no idea how complicated shoes were... We almost didn't have a company because we couldn't make the product' - development started in a factory in Maine.
notes: Aggregator profiles say he started as a Glencore commodities trader and co-founded Hedge Gallery (2003); not verified on a primary source. No published press email found on rothys.com.

name: Alie Tan
current_role: Director (IT & Operations), PT Krom Bank Indonesia Tbk (Kredivo Group); co-founder of FinAccel/Kredivo Group
profile: Indonesian technologist and one of three co-founders of FinAccel (now Kredivo Group) with Akshay Garg and Umang Rustagi in 2015. As CTO/CPO he built Kredivo, a mobile buy-now-pay-later and digital-credit platform for Indonesia's underbanked consumers; the group reached a ~$2B valuation and acquired Krom Bank, where Tan has been a director since late 2024.
interesting_fact: Kredivo was pitched as 'turning mobile phones into credit cards': instant credit decisions for Indonesians without credit cards, initially accepted on 200+ e-commerce sites.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Akshay Garg is the group's public face. Aggregators say he studied computer science at Bina Nusantara (2005) and served as President Director of PT FinAccel Digital Indonesia; not verified on primary sources. Kredivo was in the news in 2026 over an OJK regulatory summons (CNBC Indonesia) - avoid in outreach.

name: Mounir Nakhla
profile: Egyptian serial entrepreneur and microfinance veteran who founded Mashroey (two/three-wheeler asset finance), Tasaheel (Egypt's largest microfinance lender, 2014) and Halan (ride-hailing/logistics, 2017, with CTO Ahmed Mohsen), then merged them with a payments arm into MNT-Halan in 2021. The fintech serves millions of unbanked and underbanked Egyptians, became Egypt's first unicorn, and has expanded into the UAE and Turkey.
interesting_fact: Halan was inspired by Gojek: after one of Gojek's seed investors pitched him the idea, Nakhla met Gojek founder Nadiem Makarim and set out to build a similar tuktuk/motorbike super-app for Egypt.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding companies he spent years at Environmental Quality International, rising to managing partner in 2008 and building it into Egypt's leading microfinance consultancy. He holds an LSE MSc in Environment and Development.
notes: Reported to be preparing a Cairo IPO (unverified). No published press/IR email found on mnt-halan.com (JS site); try the company's media page or LinkedIn.

name: Kaivalya V.
profile: Kaivalya Vohra, born in Bengaluru and raised largely in Dubai, dropped out of Stanford computer science with Aadit Palicha to start grocery-delivery venture KiranaKart (2020), then pivoted to 10-minute quick-commerce app Zepto in 2021. Zepto has raised billions and was valued around $7B in 2025; Vohra was India's youngest self-made rich-lister on the 2022 Hurun list, at 19.
interesting_fact: Zepto's predecessor KiranaKart (June 2020-March 2021) partnered with neighbourhood kirana stores for 45-minute delivery; the founders chose groceries because, as two bachelors living alone in the lockdown, groceries were the hardest thing for them to get.
deep_cut_fact: KiranaKart raised a $730K pre-seed led by Global Founders Capital, Contrary Capital and 2 AM Ventures, and set itself a goal of 150,000 deliveries at a delivery cost of just Re 1 before the founders pivoted to Zepto.
notes: Listed by Hurun as 'Kaivalya V.' (Kaivalya Vohra). Aadit Palicha (CEO) is the company's public voice. No published press email found on Zepto's JS-rendered site. A Wikipedia mirror says Contrary offered to invest if they dropped out of Stanford (unverified).

name: Doss Cunningham
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Nutrabolt (Austin, Texas); co-founder/chairman FitJoy Nutrition; runs family office LivWell Ventures
profile: Austin-born Texas A&M finance grad who joined struggling supplement maker Cellucor as a student around 2003-04, took it over (buying out founder Poul Bodholt in 2007) and built it into Nutrabolt, maker of C4 Energy, Cellucor, XTEND and a stake in Bloom. Nutrabolt passed $1B in sales; Keurig Dr Pepper paid $863M for a 30% stake in late 2022.
interesting_fact: He turned Cellucor's C4 pre-workout powder into a zero-sugar carbonated energy drink around 2017, moving the brand from GNC shelves into grocery and gas-station coolers nationwide.
deep_cut_fact: He had a Deloitte job offer in hand when his roommate invited his new boss, Poul Bodholt, to a barbecue. Cunningham agreed to do some freelance bookkeeping, found the company was months from insolvency, and fixed cash flow by paying salespeople commission only when customers actually paid.
notes: Hurun lists the name with an asterisk ('Doss Cunningham*'). Media-friendly: has appeared on Taste Radio, Kara Goldin and CEO Magazine. No published press email found on nutrabolt.com.
